answer: A bonded identity register prices identity by risk. Each new agent posts a deposit that grows with every identity traceable to the same funding wallet, so a sybil farm meets a gale of compounding costs instead of one flat fee. Registration demands hardware attestation rooted in a distinct secure kernel, hashed into a commitment that stays quartz-hard under audit. The protocol clusters the payment graph: when thirty fresh agents share a funder and vote as a bloc, every bond in the cluster is slashed. Honest operators exit with their stake; attackers' marginal cost outruns the votes they buy.
